conceptZh: 桶形海盜先拼出一艘歪船，鸚鵡翻白眼，他聳肩一翻，拼成勇字，大聲吹號。
object: a barrel-shaped toy pirate and a stubborn parrot
morph: the pirate builds a wrong boat shape, then flips it right into 勇
creativeAngle: 先錯後對：鸚鵡不合作，反而讓勇氣更好笑。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip on a light aqua background, with one single Traditional Chinese glyph 勇 as the only text on screen, drawn in bold crimson solid strokes, centered, uncropped, about 70% of frame height with generous margins. 0-1.7s: a round barrel-bodied toy pirate with a patch and a plastic hook marches in carrying wooden stroke planks while an unimpressed green parrot on his shoulder turns its back; the first 勇 is spoken as he slams the top planks of 勇 down. 1.7-3.4s: he proudly builds the bottom 力 upside-down so the whole thing looks like a little boat, the parrot slowly faces the camera with a flat stare; the second 勇 is spoken as he notices, shrugs, and flips the part right-side-up in one quick move. 3.4-5s: 勇敢 is spoken as a toy cardboard wave splashes up, he plants his feet and puffs his barrel chest instead of ducking, and the parrot reluctantly salutes with one wing. 5-8s: hold; he keeps his chest puffed with a small happy wobble, the parrot still unimpressed, glyph still. Audio: a warm off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "勇、勇、勇敢" (ㄩㄥˇ、ㄩㄥˇ、ㄩㄥˇ ㄍㄢˇ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, a short pause between the two single utterances, and stops after the word; no other speech, no subtitles, no vocabulary text. Final 3 seconds (5-8s): the glyph 勇 is perfectly still and fully readable while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. Bright but not neon palette, no watermark, no flashing, no other writing.
